subject: Adaptive-surge & linear-scaling benchmarking questionnaire — runbook draft and clarifications
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@atlas-enterprises.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas Enterprises Procurement <procurement@atlas-enterprises.com>, Maya Rios <maya.rios@atlas-enterprises.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: adaptive surge + linear scaling benchmarks - clarifications

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick turn on the RFP packet. A few follow-ups from our performance team to help us compare vendor artifacts apples-to-apples: we need specifics on how you validate behavior across two dimensions simultaneously — (1) microburst-adaptive surge (sub-second spikes to 10x baseline) and (2) linear-scaling coefficient (throughput growth as replicas increase).

What we want from Redwood: a short runbook that explains the test harness, how you synthesize traffic for both steady-state and ramp-and-hold microbursts, the warm/cold start definitions you use, and the exact metric definitions (e.g., p50/p90/p99 server-side inference, end-to-end response, queuing delay). Can you also include a failure-injection plan to exercise graceful degradation and model-fallbacks?

If you can respond with a brief runbook + a CSV test matrix and the artifacts you’d provide post-test (raw logs, token-level latency CSVs, KV cache hit traces), we can slot this into our bakeoff next week.

Regards,
Sam
Performance Engineering
Atlas Enterprises

[Attachment: atlas_rfp_section-5.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@atlas-enterprises.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: adaptive surge + linear scaling benchmarks - clarifications

Sam —

Appreciate the level-set. Attached is a concise runbook (kimberly_performance_runbook_v1.pdf) and a starter surge_test_matrix.csv that maps scenarios to traffic profiles and pass/fail thresholds. Summary below; full details are in the PDF.

High-level test approach:
- Harness: k6-based synthetic driver + our traffic router to simulate client-side token pacing and connection fanout.
- Scenarios: baseline (steady qps), ramp (linear increase to target), microburst (sub-second spikes expressed as x*baseline for 200ms–5s), burst trains (repeat microbursts at configurable intervals), and long-soak (12h–24h).
- Warm vs cold: warm = endpoint with populated KV cache + warmed GPU kernels (>= 5 prior requests in last 60s); cold = cache-cleared, cold-start container (no prior requests for >10min). We capture both cold-start tail quantiles separately.
- Metrics collected: server_infer_ms (per-token), end2end_ms (client-observed), queue_delay_ms, kv_cache_hit_ratio, batching_latency_ms, CPU/GPU utilization, memory pressure, and error_rate_by_code. We persist raw per-request token traces.
- Scaling coefficient: we run step-scaling (1 -> N replicas) and fit throughput = a * replicas + b; coefficient a reported with confidence intervals.
- Degradation policy test: exercise model fallback (e.g., lower-capacity quantized variant) and region failover; measure latency and token-delta quality (BLEU/ROUGE on synthetic eval set).

Artifacts we provide after each run:
- raw_token_latency.csv (per-request, per-token timestamps)
- node-level metrics (Prometheus export)
- request traces (Jaeger IDs)
- surge_test_matrix.csv (scenario parameters and results)
- short executive summary with pass/fail and recommendations

Attachments included: surge_test_matrix.csv and kv_cache-impact-summary.txt (quick notes on cache priming effects). Ben, Priya — can you review the degradation policy wording and confirm the fallback sequence we list? Vivek, please mark whether we can deliver the raw token traces within the RFP NDA window.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: kimberly_performance_runbook_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Maya Rios <maya.rios@atlas-enterprises.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@atlas-enterprises.com>, Atlas Enterprises Procurement <procurement@atlas-enterprises.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: adaptive surge + linear scaling benchmarks - clarifications

Hi Kimberly — quick note from our side. Two clarifications before we schedule the bakeoff: (1) For the microburst tests we want both connection-level bursts (many short-lived connections opening simultaneously) and session-level bursts (existing connections suddenly increasing token QPS). Can your harness emulate both? (2) For the scaling coefficient, please include the deviation from linearity metric (R^2 and percent deviation at high replica counts).

Also — we need to know whether tokenization differences between model variants (e.g., different tokenizers between open models) are normalized during throughput calculation, or if you report raw tokens per model variant.

Thanks,
Maya
Senior Performance Engineer
Atlas Enterprises

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 May 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: adaptive surge + linear scaling benchmarks - clarifications

Kimberly —

Reviewed and annotated. Short answers to Atlas clarifications:
1) Harness capability: yes — our k6 driver supports both connection churn and token-rate modulation on long-lived sockets. We simulate short TCP TLS handshakes and open/close cycles for connection-spike scenarios; session-level bursts are modeled by increasing per-connection token emit rate.
2) Scaling coefficient: will include linear fit, 95% CI, R^2, and percent deviation at the top replica point. We'll add a visual residuals plot to the artifacts.
3) Tokenization normalization: we report raw tokens per model variant and include a normalized tokens-per-second metric (tokens mapped to Atlas's canonical tokenizer) when requested — we note tokenizer differences explicitly in the runbook.

Action items:
- Priya: update runbook section 3.2 to call out connection vs session burst config (deadline EOD Tue).
- Vivek: confirm policy for delivering token-level traces under NDA (if not possible, outline derived artifacts).
- Kimberly: once edits are in, push the final runbook and notify Atlas for bakeoff scheduling.

Ben
Senior Product Manager, Performance
Redwood Inference
